I’ve been feeling... off... for about three months now. One minute I’m on top of things, sharp, like I can handle anything—my wife says I’ve been talking a mile a minute, barely letting her get a word in. I’ve taken on extra shifts at the post, started calling up old coworkers just to chat, maybe plan meetups. Feels good to be out there, connected. But then, outta nowhere, I get restless, snappy. Little things set me off—a delayed radio check, the coffee machine breaking. I pace the lobby more than I should, chain-walking laps like I’m still patrolling, even when I’m off duty.

There’s this buzz in my chest, like I’m wired. Some days it’s energy, some days it’s just… tight. I don’t know if it’s worry or just momentum. I’ve been sleeping less, not because I can’t, but because my head won’t power down. My wife says I’m wound tight—too much going on at once. I don’t feel out of control, not exactly, but things are… faster. I can’t tell if the jumpiness comes from feeling anxious, or if the energy’s just carrying it along. It’s all mixed up.

It started at work—suddenly I wasn’t just staying alert, I was rearranging the entire security schedule, calling local businesses to offer extra patrols, even started planning a community safety night. My wife says I haven’t stopped talking since February. I’ll be laughing one minute, telling her grand plans about starting my own security firm, and then get furious because she doesn’t “get” the vision.

I talk so fast now, people interrupt me just to make me slow down. My shifts feel too short—I take on double hours, clean the house at 3 a.m., call old friends out of the blue. I barely sleep, but I don’t feel tired.  

Yeah, I’ve been anxious too—heart racing, constantly checking locks, worrying about money. But the thoughts aren’t about worry—they just *fly*, like I can’t catch them. The ideas come before I even know I had them. I’ll book a flight or sign up for a course without thinking. The anxiety doesn’t *cause* that—it’s just there, but the speeding mind and the acting first, thinking later? That’s its own thing. It was like a switch flipped, and I couldn’t turn it off.

It’s like my thoughts are racing, but only because I’m obsessing over all these “what ifs.” I’ll start ten things at once—cleaning the garage, calling old friends, redoing the budget—but not because I feel great or unstoppable, but because I can’t sit still with the worry.  

I’ve been talking fast, sure—my wife says I’m impossible to interrupt—but it’s because I’m trying to get everything out before I forget, or before something bad happens. I’ve been calling people out of the blue, not because I’m suddenly outgoing, but I feel like I need someone to tell me I’m not failing somewhere. The mood swings? One minute I’m trying to reassure myself, the next I’m snapping at my wife because I feel like everything’s unraveling. But it’s never a high—just anxiety masquerading as energy. The thoughts race *because* I’m anxious, not in spite of it.
